popup.deep: Deep analysis with my UniPhish server
popup.deep_off: Deep analysis is off. Turn it on in Settings and add your server address.
popup.local: Local or private address — not checked.
popup.invalid: That does not look like a web address.

inter.lead: UniPhish stopped this link because it looks like a phishing attempt.
inter.heading: Why this link is dangerous
inter.confirm: I understand this site may steal my passwords or money.
inter.report_gsb: Report to Google Safe Browsing (opens another site)

opt.title: UniPhish settings
opt.scan_links: Mark risky links on web pages
opt.scan_links_help: Outlines links that look suspicious or dangerous. Runs entirely on your device.
opt.intercept: Show a warning page before opening dangerous links
opt.nav: Also warn when I open a dangerous address directly
opt.nav_help: Needs the extra “webNavigation” permission; your browser will ask you to allow it.
opt.threshold_help: Lower values catch more phishing but cause more false alarms. Defaults: 50% and 85%.
opt.trusted_help: One domain per line. Links to these sites are never marked.
opt.deep_help: Off by default. When on, the popup can send a URL you scan to your own UniPhish server for a full analysis. Nothing is ever sent automatically.
opt.apikey_help: Stored only in this browser profile.
opt.endpoint_invalid: Enter a full address such as https://uniphish.example.com
opt.endpoint_http: Plain http is only allowed for localhost.
opt.privacy: Privacy: all link scoring happens inside your browser. The only network request this extension can ever make is the optional deep analysis above.
r.brand.homoglyph: The domain imitates {brand} with look-alike letters: “{label}” reads as “{term}”.
r.brand.homoglyph.char: This link uses the {script} letter “{char}” ({cp}) to look like “{like}” — it imitates {brand} ({legit}).
r.brand.idn.char: This link uses the {script} letter “{char}” ({cp}) to look like “{like}” and imitates {brand}.
r.brand.typosquat: The domain is a misspelling or look-alike of {brand}’s name (“{term}”).
r.brand.bitsquat: The domain differs from {brand}’s by a single flipped bit (“{term}”).
r.brand.combosquat: The domain combines the name {brand} with extra words to look official (“{label}”).
r.brand.subdomain: {brand}’s name is used as a sub-domain, but the real site is {registrable}.
r.brand.path: {brand}’s name appears in the page path, but this is not a {brand} website.
r.unicode.confusable_host: The address uses letters that look like Latin ones: {chars}.
r.unicode.confusable_host.char: The address uses the {script} letter “{char}” ({cp}) to look like “{like}”.
r.unicode.skeleton_matches_top_domain: The domain looks identical to a popular site once look-alike letters are normalised.
r.unicode.whole_script_confusable: A whole part of the domain is written in {script} letters that read as Latin letters.
r.unicode.mixed_script_host: The domain mixes alphabets ({scripts}), a classic spoofing trick.
r.unicode.bidi_control: The domain contains text-direction control characters that can reorder what you see.
r.unicode.dangerous_char: The domain contains characters that imitate “/” or “.” to fake the address structure.
r.unicode.combining_mark: The domain stacks accent marks on Latin letters to disguise them.
r.unicode.digit_lookalike: The domain uses letters that look like digits.
r.unicode.punycode_lookalike: The punycode address {host} decodes to a look-alike of another site: “{unicode}”.
r.unicode.punycode: The address uses punycode (xn--), which encodes non-Latin characters.
r.url.ip_host: The link goes to a raw IP address ({ip}) instead of a website name.
r.url.ip_obfuscation: The IP address is disguised in an unusual number format ({raw} → {ip}).
r.url.at_redirect: The text before “@” (“{userinfo}”) is a decoy; the link really goes to {host}.
r.url.shortener: {host} is a link shortener; the real destination is hidden.
r.url.dynamic_dns: {host} is on a free dynamic-DNS service that anyone can use.
r.url.lots_hosting: Hosted on {platform}, a free platform anyone can publish on.
r.url.open_redirect: The “{param}” parameter forwards you to another site ({dest}).
r.url.suspicious_tld: The “.{tld}” ending is heavily used by phishing sites.
r.url.many_subdomains: {count} sub-domain labels push the real domain out of view.
r.url.credential_lure_host: The address contains sign-in or security words: {words}.
r.url.credential_lure_path: The path contains sign-in or security words: {words}.
r.url.suspicious_file_ext: The link downloads a {ext} file, a type often used to spread malware.
r.url.double_extension: The file name hides its real type ({ext}) behind a harmless-looking extension.
r.url.dangerous_scheme: The link uses the “{scheme}:” scheme, which runs or embeds content directly.
r.url.double_encoding: The link is encoded twice to hide its content.
r.url.random_label: A part of the address looks randomly generated.
r.url.non_standard_port: The link uses an unusual port ({port}).
r.url.long_url: The address is very long ({len} characters), which can hide where it goes.
r.url.many_hyphens: The domain has {count} hyphens, a common squatting pattern.
r.rep.top_site: {domain} is one of the most visited sites on the web.
r.rep.user_allowlist: You marked {domain} as a trusted site.
r.ml.cnn.phishing: The on-device AI model rates this address {pct}% likely to be phishing.
r.ml.cnn.benign: The on-device AI model finds this address looks ordinary ({pct}% phishing likelihood).
